title: On-air etiquette
idea: Nobody owns a frequency. Ask before you call, break in with just your call sign, answer distress first, and work out conflicts politely.

items: CW: QRL? and your call. Phone: ask if it is in use, and your call
No one has it, except in emergencies
Acknowledge, find out what help is needed
Work it out with the other stations
Only stations outside the lower 48 answer
So each station can operate according to conditions

config.heading: You are on the air
config.lead: Pick a situation, then what you would do.

dims.label: You...
options: Say Breaker Breaker
Say your call sign once
Say QRZ several times, then your call sign
Say CQ and one station's call sign

do: Say your call sign once

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Wait for a pause and say your call sign once. The stations will acknowledge you.

do: Say Breaker Breaker

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Breaker Breaker is CB talk, not amateur practice.

do: Say QRZ several times, then your call sign

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: QRZ asks who is calling me; it does not get you in.

do: Say CQ and one station's call sign

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: CQ is a general call, not a way into an existing contact.

situations.label: Someone in Ohio calls CQ DX
situations.title: Someone in Ohio calls CQ DX

dims.label: You...
options: Anyone answers
Only contest stations answer
Only stations outside the lower 48 answer

do: Only stations outside the lower 48 answer

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: CQ DX from the lower 48 means the caller wants distant stations: anyone outside the contiguous 48 states.

do: Anyone answers

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Not anyone: the caller asked for DX.

do: Only contest stations answer

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: DX is about distance, not contests.

situations.label: A net says it needs your frequency
situations.title: A net says it needs your frequency

dims.label: You...
options: Nets have priority, so you must move
No one has priority except in emergencies
Contacts in progress have priority, so stay

do: No one has priority except in emergencies

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency. Moving to help out is courteous, but nobody owns it.

do: Nets have priority, so you must move

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Nets have no special priority.

do: Contacts in progress have priority, so stay

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Being there first gives no priority either.

situations.label: A station in distress breaks in
situations.title: A station in distress breaks in

dims.label: You...
options: Stop transmitting
Call your emergency coordinator
Turn your power down
Acknowledge them and find out what help is needed

do: Acknowledge them and find out what help is needed

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Acknowledge the station in distress first and determine what assistance may be needed. Everything else comes after.

do: Stop transmitting

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Going silent leaves them with nobody.

do: Call your emergency coordinator

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: That may come later; acknowledge them first.

do: Turn your power down

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Turning down does not help them.

situations.label: Propagation shifts and others now share your frequency
situations.title: Propagation shifts and others now share your frequency

dims.label: You...
options: Tell them you have priority
Switch to the opposite sideband
Work it out with them in a mutually acceptable way
Turn power down and keep going

do: Work it out with them in a mutually acceptable way

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Attempt to resolve the interference with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner. Neither of you has priority.

do: Tell them you have priority

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Nobody has priority.

do: Switch to the opposite sideband

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: That just puts you on top of someone else.

do: Turn power down and keep going

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Continuing on top of them doesn't resolve anything.

situations.label: The frequency sounds clear and you want to call CQ
situations.title: The frequency sounds clear and you want to call CQ

dims.label: Mode
options: CW
Phone

dims.label: You...
options: Listen 2 minutes, then call
Ask if it is in use, with your call sign
Send V or say test several times
Send QSY or announce it is in use

do: Ask if it is in use, with your call sign

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: On CW, send QRL? followed by your call sign. You may only be hearing one side of a contact.

do: Ask if it is in use, with your call sign

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: On phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign.

do: Listen 2 minutes, then call

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Listening first is good, but only asking tells you about the side you cannot hear.

do: Send V or say test several times

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Test transmissions on a busy band are just interference.

do: Send QSY or announce it is in use

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: QSY means change frequency, and it is not your frequency to announce.

dims.label: You...
options: Follow the voluntary band plan
Send your call sign 3 times first
Listen at least two minutes

do: Follow the voluntary band plan

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Follow the voluntary band plan: put your mode where others expect it.

do: Send your call sign 3 times first

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Identification rules don't pick a frequency.

do: Listen at least two minutes

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Not a rule, and not what picks the frequency.

dims.label: You...
options: CQ a few times, this is, your call a few times, then listen
Your call once and listening for a call
QTC, this is, your call
An unmodulated carrier for 10 seconds, then your call

do: CQ a few times, this is, your call a few times, then listen

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Repeat CQ a few times, then this is and your call sign a few times, then pause to listen. Repeat as needed.

do: Your call once and listening for a call

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Too short: nobody tuning by will catch it.

do: QTC, this is, your call

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: QTC is about traffic (messages), not a general call.

do: An unmodulated carrier for 10 seconds, then your call

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: A plain carrier is interference.

dims.label: You...
options: Exchange reports so each can adjust
Exchange reports so it counts for awards
Exchange reports to calibrate the dial

do: Exchange reports so each can adjust

rules.title: Good practice
rules.text: Signal reports at the start let each station operate according to conditions: slow down, repeat, change power or move.

do: Exchange reports so it counts for awards

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Awards need confirmations, not reports.

do: Exchange reports to calibrate the dial

rules.title: Not this one
rules.text: Reports say nothing about frequency.

traps.why: CB habit. On amateur bands you say your call sign once.

traps.wrong: Any caller is welcome to respond
traps.why: CQ DX asks for distant stations only.
Nets don't get priority. Only emergencies do.
Going silent abandons the station in distress. Acknowledge them first.

traps.wrong: Advise the interfering stations that you are on the frequency and that you have priority
traps.why: Nobody has priority, so you can't claim it.

traps.wrong: Listen for 2 minutes before calling CQ
traps.why: Listening is good, but you may only hear one side. Ask.
Only the band plan picks the frequency.

traps.wrong: Transmit an unmodulated carried for approximately 10 seconds, followed by “this is” and your call sign, and pause to listen -- repeat as necessary
traps.why: A plain carrier is just interference.

traps.wrong: To be sure the contact will count for award programs
traps.why: Reports are about operating to conditions, not awards.
